quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Priya and her manager, Ms. Osei, met on Monday to discuss the quarterly report. She had prepared a draft over the weekend, but Ms. Osei asked her to shorten it and add a summary page for the board. After the meeting, Priya spent two days revising it, and on Wednesday she sent it back with a note explaining the changes. Ms. Osei replied that it was much clearer and approved it for circulation the next morning.
quests.question: Who wrote the first draft of the report?
quests.hint: In "She had prepared a draft", check which person the next clause treats as the one being asked to shorten it.
quests.explanation: Ms. Osei asks "her" to shorten the draft, so the earlier "She" must be Priya. Tracking who is being asked and who is asking resolves the pronoun.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Scientists studying the lake found that its water had become murkier over twenty years. At first they blamed farm fertiliser, which can feed algae. But when they measured the chemicals, they found levels of these substances were falling. The real culprit, they now believe, is heavier rainfall, which washes soil into the water from the surrounding hills. This finding matters because it changes what local authorities should do: controlling farm chemicals alone will not clear the lake.
quests.question: What does "This finding" refer to?
options: Rain carrying soil into the lake is the main cause
The lake is getting deeper because of erosion
Farm chemicals are increasing year after year
Algae grow only during the winter months
quests.correctAnswer: Rain carrying soil into the lake is the main cause
quests.hint: A demonstrative phrase usually points to the idea in the sentence just before it.
quests.explanation: "This finding" refers to the new belief about rainfall and soil in the previous sentence. The fertiliser idea was the earlier, rejected explanation.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The company's engineers designed the new charger and tested it against three older models. The whole project took nine months and involved a team of six. The older ones, they found, wasted energy as heat, whereas theirs lost far less. Sales staff were delighted, but the engineers were more cautious. They pointed out that the tests took place in a cool laboratory and that results in hot climates might differ. That, they said, was the next thing to check.
quests.question: What does "That" refer to at the end?
options: How the older chargers were built
How the charger performs in hot climates
quests.correctAnswer: How the charger performs in hot climates
quests.hint: Ask what the engineers said might differ, and look one sentence back.
quests.explanation: "That" points to the possibility that hot-climate results might differ. The laboratory temperature is the reason for the doubt, not the thing to check.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Hana booked a small guesthouse in Kyoto for herself and her brother. It was cheap and close to the station, but when they arrived, they found that the two single beds she had requested had been replaced by one double. The owner apologised and offered them a larger room the following night at no extra charge. Hana accepted, though her brother complained that he would have preferred a different guesthouse altogether. In the end, they stayed two nights and spent most of their time visiting temples.
quests.question: Who would have preferred a different guesthouse?
quests.hint: The last sentence has two people with "her" and "he". Sort out who is who.
quests.explanation: "Her brother complained that he would have preferred..." makes the brother the one who wanted somewhere else. Hana was the one who accepted.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Electric buses are quieter than diesel ones, and they produce no fumes on the street. Yet the latter remain common because they cost far less to buy. Transport planners argue that this gap will narrow as battery prices fall, and that savings on fuel already cover part of the difference. Charging stations at depots are also being built so that buses can recharge overnight. Until then, many cities are buying a mixture of the two.
quests.question: What does "the latter" refer to?
quests.hint: "The latter" means the last of two things just mentioned.
quests.explanation: Two types are named, electric then diesel, so "the latter" is diesel. Only diesel buses are described as cheaper to buy.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The museum's director spoke to the press on Tuesday about the stolen painting. According to her, it had been insured for two million dollars, but its cultural value was much greater. Investigators believe the thief entered through a rooftop window and knew exactly which alarm to disable. They have released images from a camera across the road and are asking anyone who recognises the person to come forward. Police say the alarm system was installed only two years ago.
quests.question: Who has released images from a camera?
quests.hint: Look for the last plural group named before the pronoun.
quests.explanation: The plural subject before "They" is the investigators, who are the people trying to identify the thief. The director is a single person.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: When Mr. Ferreira opened a restaurant, he hired a chef named Leila and gave her freedom to design the menu. Her cooking quickly attracted critics, and within a year the place was fully booked every weekend. Then a rival offered her a better salary, and she left. Mr. Ferreira was upset, but he promoted her assistant, Jonas, who had learned many of her recipes. The restaurant is still busy, although some regulars say it is not quite the same.
quests.question: Whose recipes had Jonas learned?
quests.hint: Follow "her" back to the last woman mentioned before it.
quests.explanation: "Her assistant" and "her recipes" both refer to Leila, the chef who left. Mr. Ferreira is the owner.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Hospitals are complicated places, and moving supplies around them takes up a surprising amount of staff time. Many hospitals now use robots to move supplies. These machines follow marked routes and avoid obstacles using sensors, freeing nurses from carrying heavy boxes. Patients rarely notice them, but staff do: one nurse said she used to walk several kilometres a shift, and that this had ended. However, they cannot open certain doors without help, which sometimes causes small traffic jams in the corridors.
quests.question: What had ended for the nurse?
options: Noticing the robots as they moved around the ward
Walking long distances while carrying supplies
Using sensors to avoid obstacles in the corridors
Opening doors for patients who needed help
quests.correctAnswer: Walking long distances while carrying supplies
quests.hint: Look at what the nurse said she "used to" do.
quests.explanation: "This" refers to the habit of walking several kilometres a shift. The robots took over the carrying, so it stopped.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Two towns, Alder and Birch, share a river. For most of the last century, it was the only thing they had in common. In the past, Alder's factories polluted it, and Birch's fishermen complained for decades. Now Alder has installed filters, and Birch has begun a small festival celebrating the river's return to health. Their councils, once bitter rivals, are planning to share the cost of a riverside path. It will link the towns, and both hope it will draw visitors.
quests.question: What does the first "It" in the last sentence refer to?
quests.hint: A verb like "link" limits what the subject can be. What can join two towns?
quests.explanation: A path can connect two places, unlike a festival or a filter. The nearest thing mentioned before "It" is the path itself.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Dr. Thomas Mbeki and Dr. Ingrid Lindqvist co-wrote a study on urban noise. He collected the data across six cities, while she analysed how it affected sleep. Their findings, published last month, show that residents on busy streets wake more often at night, though most of them are unaware of it. The authors recommend triple-glazed windows and lower speed limits, which they say would be cheaper than treating the health problems that follow.
quests.question: Who analysed the effect of noise on sleep?
quests.hint: Match the pronouns to the first names.
quests.explanation: "He" is Thomas Mbeki, who collected the data, and "she" is Ingrid Lindqvist, who analysed sleep. Gender words are the key to the pairing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The council wants to replace the old swimming pool, which is expensive to heat and often closed for repairs. One proposal is to build a new pool on the same site; the other is to convert the disused factory nearby. The first would be faster, but the second, supporters say, would give the town a leisure centre and save the historic building. Either way, residents will have no pool for at least two years.
quests.question: What does "the second" refer to?
options: Building a new pool on the same site
Heating the old pool more cheaply
quests.hint: Two proposals are numbered by position. Which one came second?
quests.explanation: The first proposal is a new pool on the same site, and the other, the second, is the factory conversion. Only that option would also save a historic building.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Our new hire, Kwame, spent his first week shadowing Amara in customer support. She showed him how to use the ticket system and let him listen to calls, which he found valuable. Amara, who has worked in the team for six years, says she learned as much from explaining things as he did from listening. By Friday, he was answering simple questions himself, with her checking his replies. Their manager says this approach works better than a day of classroom training, and it will now be used for every newcomer.
quests.question: What is "this approach"?
options: Studying the ticket system online at home
Learning by working beside an experienced colleague
A day of classroom training for every newcomer
Answering questions alone from the first day
quests.correctAnswer: Learning by working beside an experienced colleague
quests.hint: The whole first half of the passage describes the approach. Summarise it in your own words.
quests.explanation: Kwame followed Amara, listened to calls and gradually took over, so the method is learning alongside an experienced colleague. It is contrasted with classroom training.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: When the city council announced plans for a tram line, business owners along the route were divided. Some welcomed it, expecting more customers; others feared years of construction noise and blocked pavements. To address the second group's worries, the council promised compensation and a strict schedule of works. Nevertheless, many remain unconvinced, saying that promises are easy to make and difficult to keep. A public meeting will be held next month so that owners can question the engineers directly.
quests.question: Whose worries did the council try to address?
options: Tram drivers who feared losing their jobs
Shoppers on the route who wanted a new stop
Owners hoping for more customers after the tram opens
quests.hint: Work out which of the two groups is called "the second".
quests.explanation: The first group welcomed the tram and the second feared construction problems. Compensation and a strict schedule respond to those fears.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Modern thermometers no longer use mercury, a liquid metal that is toxic if it escapes. Instead, they rely on digital sensors or coloured alcohol, both of which are safer. Older ones are still found in many homes, and health agencies ask that they be taken to collection points rather than thrown away. Some pharmacies will exchange an old thermometer for a digital one at a small charge. Those who have broken one should ventilate the room and avoid vacuuming the spill.
quests.question: What does "both of which" refer to?
quests.hint: The phrase comes right after a pair joined by "or".
quests.explanation: "Both of which are safer" describes the two replacements just listed. Mercury is presented as the unsafe option they replaced.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: My grandfather kept a small notebook in which he wrote every train he ever took, noting the date, the route and often the weather. After he died, my cousin Elena inherited it. She has since spent months turning its entries into a map of his journeys, and she plans to display it at the family reunion. For me, the notebook was never as interesting as the stories he told from it. Someday I may read it properly, but for now I am happy that it is in good hands.
quests.question: Who plans to display the map at the reunion?
quests.hint: Follow "she" back to the last woman named.
quests.explanation: "She" is the cousin Elena, who inherited the notebook and made the map. The grandfather has died, and the narrator is the writer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The town's museum recently acquired a set of letters written by a sailor to his wife in the 1850s. Historians say they offer rare details of daily life on board, such as food rations and illness. The museum plans to publish transcripts of all forty letters online next year. Because the paper is fragile, only copies are displayed; the originals are stored in a controlled room. Visitors who want to see them must apply in advance, and requests are approved only for research.
quests.question: What must visitors apply in advance to see?
quests.hint: The word "them" follows a contrast between two versions of the letters.
quests.explanation: Copies are on display, so applying is needed only for the originals. "Them" refers to the stored originals mentioned just before.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Two teachers, one from a state school and one from a private academy, swapped classrooms for a term. The former found that her pupils were more diverse and less used to individual attention; the latter discovered that class sizes were larger than he had imagined. Both agreed that the exchange had changed how they explain difficult ideas. The school heads plan to repeat the exchange next year, and each teacher has kept a diary that will be published in a teaching journal.
quests.question: Who found the classes bigger than expected?
options: The teacher from the state school
The teacher from the private academy
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher from the private academy
quests.hint: "The former" and "the latter" pick from the two teachers in the first sentence.
quests.explanation: The latter is the second teacher mentioned, from the private academy. He had imagined smaller classes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Investors were surprised when the company reported a small profit rather than the loss that most analysts had predicted. Its chief executive credited a cost-cutting programme begun last year, in which the firm closed three warehouses and merged two departments. That, however, is not sustainable, warned one analyst; she said that revenue must grow soon if the improvement is to last. Shares rose by four percent on the news, and trading was busier than usual.
quests.question: What does "That" refer to?
quests.hint: The analyst's warning is about the thing the executive credited.
quests.explanation: The executive credited cost cutting, and the analyst says that cannot continue forever. Revenue growth is her proposed remedy.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The village school, closed in 2010, has been given a second life. A group of parents bought the building, repaired its roof and now runs it as a community hub. In the mornings it hosts a playgroup, and in the afternoons a computer club for older residents. The volunteers who run these activities say their aim is not profit but to keep the village from losing its centre. On Saturdays the hall is also rented out for weddings, which helps to pay the heating bills.
quests.question: What does "its" refer to in "losing its centre"?
quests.hint: Ask which noun could sensibly have a "centre" that it might lose.
quests.explanation: The volunteers want to stop the village from losing its centre. The school building is the tool, not the owner of the centre.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: A recent report, based on interviews with two hundred employees in nine countries, examined how remote teams communicate. Some rely on messages, others on video calls, and a few on shared documents. It found that teams using a mix of all three reported the fewest misunderstandings, though the authors warned that too many channels can overwhelm people. Their advice: agree in advance which tool is used for what. Such an agreement, they say, matters more than the tools themselves.
quests.question: What does "Such an agreement" refer to?
options: Choosing video calls as the only tool
Using all three tools at once for every message
Deciding which tool serves which purpose
Reporting every misunderstanding to the managers
quests.correctAnswer: Deciding which tool serves which purpose
quests.hint: The advice after the colon is what "such an agreement" points back to.
quests.explanation: The advice was to agree beforehand which tool is used for what, and that is the agreement. The mix of tools is a separate finding.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Nadia's flight from Doha to Nairobi was cancelled, and the airline offered her a seat on the next day's departure. She refused because she had a meeting the following morning. Instead, she accepted a longer route through Addis Ababa, which arrived that same evening. It cost the airline more, but they preferred it to a full refund; for her, the extra four hours of travel were the price of keeping her appointment.
quests.question: What cost the airline more?
options: Rebooking her on a longer route
quests.correctAnswer: Rebooking her on a longer route
quests.hint: Think about which action the airline chose over a full refund.
quests.explanation: "It" refers to the longer route through Addis Ababa, which the airline preferred to refunding her. The next-day seat was refused.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: In the 1990s, the town's steelworks employed nearly half its residents. When it closed, unemployment soared, and many families moved away. Empty buildings stood for years, and the site was fenced off. Yet the site's vast halls have since become a market, a climbing centre and studios for artists. This change did not happen overnight, and older residents still remember what came before, but newcomers who fill the halls know it only as a place of creativity.
quests.question: What does "it" refer to in "know it only as a place of creativity"?
options: The market hall built in the old halls
The town as a whole in the 1990s
quests.hint: The pronoun follows a mention of "the halls" and "what came before".
quests.explanation: "It" is the site of the old steelworks, which older residents remember differently. Newcomers see only its present creative use.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Diana asked her neighbour Mr. Kato to water her plants while she was away. He agreed, but when she returned, half of them had wilted. He explained that he had followed the instructions on the card she left, which recommended a cup of water daily. Only then did she realise that the card was for her indoor plants, not the ones on her balcony, which needed much more. She now writes the instructions for each pot on a separate label.
quests.question: What caused the plants to wilt?
options: Mr. Kato forgetting to water them while she was away
Too much water given to each plant every day
A hot week on the balcony that dried the soil
quests.hint: Notice which plants "which" points to in the last clause.
quests.explanation: The card suited the indoor plants, while the balcony plants needed much more. Mr. Kato followed the card correctly, so the mistake lay in the instructions.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Public libraries and coffee shops are both places where people study, but they are not the same. The former lend books and offer quiet, whereas the latter provide drinks and a background hum that some find helpful. Students often move between them, depending on the task. For reading and careful writing they choose the library; for brainstorming with friends, the cafe. Some students use both in one day, starting at the library and finishing in a cafe once their reading is done.
quests.question: Which place offers a background hum?
quests.hint: Decode "the former" and "the latter" before looking at the options.
quests.explanation: The former is libraries and the latter is coffee shops. The hum is attached to "the latter".

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The mayor, who has led the city for twelve years, announced on Monday that she would not seek re-election. Her deputy, Mr. Osei, is expected to run in her place. He has already won the support of several unions, though he faces criticism from those who believe the city needs new ideas. She declined to endorse anyone, saying only that voters should judge candidates by their plans. Voters will choose her successor in November, and campaigns are expected to begin in September.
quests.question: Who declined to endorse a candidate?
quests.hint: Gender pronouns help here: one man and one woman are mentioned.
quests.explanation: "She" is the mayor, and "he" is her deputy, Mr. Osei. The mayor stepped back and did not name a favourite.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Scientists placed tiny trackers on twenty seals to learn where they feed. They discovered that the animals travel much farther than expected, sometimes two hundred kilometres from shore. Several of them visited the same feeding areas again and again. The trackers, which weigh less than a coin, fall off when the seals shed their fur in summer. This limits the research, since it means data can only be gathered for a few months at a time.
quests.question: What limits the research?
options: A lack of seals available to study in summer
The seals travelling too far from the shore
The trackers being tiny and hard to attach
The trackers dropping off when fur is shed
quests.correctAnswer: The trackers dropping off when fur is shed
quests.hint: "This" sums up the whole of the previous sentence.
quests.explanation: "This" refers to the trackers falling off in summer, which restricts data collection. The distances the seals swim are a finding, not a limit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: When Ravi moved to the city, he shared a flat with two students, Lena and Omar. She studied medicine, he studied music, and their schedules rarely matched. Ravi soon discovered that the flat was quiet only in the mornings, when Omar was asleep. By evening, the sound of his cello filled the rooms, and Lena, who needed silence to memorise, often moved to the library. Ravi, who works nights, says he has learned to sleep through most things.
quests.question: Who played the cello?
quests.hint: Two "he" pronouns appear early. Check which man is said to study music.
quests.explanation: Omar studied music, was asleep in the mornings and had the cello in the evenings. Ravi is the newcomer and Lena studies medicine.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Dear Ms. Hartley, thank you for your letter regarding the delayed refund. We have checked your account and found that the payment was issued on 2 March, but it was sent to your previous bank account, which you closed in January. The bank returned it to us, and we are now waiting for the details of your new one. As soon as you provide them, we will send the money within three working days. We apologise for the confusion.
quests.question: Why did the refund not reach Ms. Hartley?
options: The company forgot to issue the payment in March
Her new bank returned the money to the sender
She gave incorrect details earlier this month
It was sent to an account that no longer existed
quests.correctAnswer: It was sent to an account that no longer existed
quests.hint: Follow "which" and "it" carefully; two accounts are involved.
quests.explanation: The payment went to the old account she closed in January, and the bank returned it. The company did issue it, and the "new one" has not yet been supplied.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Some people learn languages best by speaking from the first day; others prefer to build a foundation in grammar before talking. The first group often gain confidence quickly but repeat mistakes they never notice. The second may be accurate yet hesitate to speak. Teachers who combine both, encouraging conversation while correcting patterns, report the strongest results. Such balance takes planning, they admit, but learners who experience it usually keep going for longer.
quests.question: Which learners may hesitate to speak?
options: Those who speak from day one
quests.hint: Translate "the second" into one of the two kinds of learner described first.
quests.explanation: The second group is the learners who build a grammar foundation first, and they are described as accurate but hesitant. The first group gains confidence quickly.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The festival organisers had planned everything for an outdoor stage, but the forecast promised heavy rain. After a tense meeting, they moved the concerts to the sports hall next door, which holds only half as many people. They sold no additional tickets to make up for this; instead, they streamed the shows online for free. The decision cost them money, but it earned praise from fans, many of whom said it was what made them come back the following year.
quests.question: What did fans say made them return the following year?
options: The higher ticket prices charged for the second year
The heavy rain, which forced a change of stage
The way the organisers handled the change of plans
The smaller sports hall, which made the shows feel more intimate
quests.correctAnswer: The way the organisers handled the change of plans
quests.hint: Ask what "it" refers to: the decision, not the weather.
quests.explanation: "The decision" is the subject, and fans praised how the problem was handled. The hall was smaller, but that was a drawback, not a reason to return.
